title: Define analysis plan + decision thresholds for Lifecycle Growth Experiments sprint
creator: Henry Cho
project: Lifecycle Growth Experiments Sprint (Activation + Early Retention)
description:
## Context
We’re running a 3-week lifecycle growth experiments sprint to lift:
- Activation: first successful production-like inference call (agreed milestone per PM-412)
- Early retention: repeat usage in week 1–2 (D7/D14)

This ticket defines:
1) The analysis plan (windows, metrics, slices, exclusions)
2) Sample size expectations / heuristics
3) Decision thresholds (“ship / iterate / rollback”) for each experiment
4) Guardrail interpretation rules and escalation

Scope covers three levers:
- Onboarding emails (sequence + variants)
- Console nudges (checklist + banners, behind flag)
- Retargeting (LinkedIn/Google + landing page variant)

## Primary metrics (per sprint)
### Primary (Activation)
**Activation Rate @ 72h** = % of new self-serve signups that fire `first_request_success` within 72 hours of `signup_completed`.
- Also report Activation Rate @ 24h as a leading indicator.
- Secondary time metric: **Time-to-First-Success (TTFS)** in minutes (median + p75).

### Primary (Early retention)
**D7 Retention** = % of activated users who fire any “usage” event on day 7 (calendar-day, local to user’s first activation day).
- Also report D14 Retention for directional read.

### Secondary (higher-intent milestones)
Report as secondary / decision-supporting metrics (do not ship solely on these unless explicitly called out):
- `billing_added`
- `route_created` / `deployment_created`
- `token_usage_7d` (bucketed) / `requests_7d`
- `teammate_invited`

## Randomization + attribution
### Console nudges
- Randomization unit: **user_id** (sticky bucketing) via ENG-2842 middleware.
- Holdout: **10% global holdout** for baseline drift detection (if available; otherwise 5%).
- Eligibility: new signups + non-activated users only (exclude already-activated returning users).

### Email experiments
- Randomization unit: **user_id** (at send time) if tool supports; otherwise randomize at “enter sequence” event.
- Suppressions applied per deliverability plan (Marketing Ops).
- Attribution: email click-through events will be used for diagnostic cuts only; primary reads are ITT (intent-to-treat) by assignment.

### Retargeting
- Primary read is **incremental lift** where we can implement holdout; otherwise report directional performance with clear caveats.
- Where holdout not possible, use:
  - Pre/post with matched cohorts by signup week
  - Report CTR/CVR as marketing KPIs, not product activation KPIs

## Experiment read windows
### Activation read
- For each user, start clock at `signup_completed`.
- Measure:
  - Activation @ 24h and @ 72h
  - TTFS (median, p75)

### Retention read
- Start clock at `first_request_success` (activation event) for retention denominators.
- D7 and D14 measured as “any usage event” on that day.

### Fixed analysis cut
- Freeze a first pass read at **end of Week 2** (iteration point) and final read at **end of Week 3**.
- If sample sizes are small, report with wide CIs and avoid binary decisions unless lift is large and guardrails are clean.

## Data quality & exclusions
Exclude users from primary analysis if any of the following apply:
- Missing `signup_completed` timestamp
- Internal/test accounts (employee domains, load tests)
- Obvious bot behavior (see Mei Lin’s filter rules; TBD: list of heuristics)
- Duplicate user_id merges in first 24h (report count)

Event QA must be green before launch reads:
- `api_key_created`
- `first_request_success` (2xx completion)
- `first_streaming_success` (if used as diagnostic)
- `dashboard_viewed`
- UTM properties present on events when applicable (ENG-2844)

## Sample size expectations (heuristics)
We are not doing a long-running, perfectly-powered RCT here; goal is to make a good decision quickly with guardrails.

### Minimum denominators before calling a winner (rule-of-thumb)
- Activation @ 72h: prefer **>= 1,000 eligible users per arm** OR **>= 300 activations per arm** (whichever comes first).
- TTFS: prefer **>= 200 activated users per arm**.
- D7: prefer **>= 500 activated users per arm** OR run until end of sprint and treat as directional.

### What effect sizes are “meaningful” (MDE targets)
Use baseline from activation funnel sheet; until final baseline is confirmed, use these targets:
- Activation @ 72h: target lift **+8–12% relative** (e.g., 25% -> 27–28%)
- TTFS: target reduction **-10–20%** in median
- D7 retention: target lift **+5–10% relative**

If we see <5% relative lift on activation with clean guardrails, treat as “no meaningful impact” unless we have strong qualitative evidence and a clear next iteration.

## Decision thresholds (Ship / Iterate / Rollback)
### Global principles
- Decisions are based on the **primary metric for that lever** (activation @72h for onboarding; D7 for retention-focused changes).
- We ship only if:
  1) Primary metric improves beyond threshold AND
  2) Guardrails are green AND
  3) No major data-quality flags

### Console nudges (checklist + banners)
**Ship / expand rollout** if:
- Activation @ 72h improves **>= +8% relative** vs control (or >= +2.0pp absolute if baseline >= 25%), AND
- TTFS median does not worsen by >5%, AND
- No statistically/operationally meaningful regression in console performance (SLO guardrail), AND
- Support-link click rate + support ticket volume do not spike beyond guardrail limits.

**Iterate** if:
- Activation lift is between +2% and +8% relative and guardrails are green, OR
- Activation lift is strong but a specific segment regresses (e.g., Python SDK users) and we have a plausible fix (copy/rules).

**Rollback** if any:
- Activation @72h decreases by **>= -5% relative** OR
- Console performance guardrail trips (see below) OR
- Support tickets related to onboarding/console confusion rise sharply and are clearly attributable.

### Email sequence
**Ship (keep sequence default-on for eligible cohort)** if:
- Activation @ 72h improves **>= +6% relative**, AND
- Unsubscribe rate + complaint rate remain within guardrails.

**Iterate** if:
- Open rate/CTR improves but activation lift is < +6% relative (optimize CTA / targeting / send time).

**Rollback / pause** if:
- Unsubscribe rate exceeds guardrail threshold for 2 consecutive send days OR
- Any confirmed suppression/opt-out compliance incident.

### Retargeting
**Ship (increase budget / broaden audiences)** if:
- Landing page CVR and cost-per-activated-user improve vs current baseline by **>= 15%**, AND
- Downstream activation quality (TTFS, error rate) does not degrade.

**Iterate** if:
- CTR improves but CVR is flat (creative mismatch), or CVR improves but activation quality degrades (landing page expectations mis-set).

**Pause** if:
- Significant increase in low-quality signups/bots or measurable support noise.

## Guardrails (with concrete thresholds)
Owner: Sean Gallagher (SLO), Dev Patel (Support), Tyler Benson (Deliverability)

### Email deliverability & compliance
- Unsubscribe rate: **> 1.2%** on any email OR **> 0.8%** sustained over 3 sends => investigate; if >1.2% for 2 sends => pause variant.
- Spam complaint rate: any meaningful spike (tool-defined) => pause and review copy/targeting.
- Any suppression/opt-out bug (e.g., SUP-2849 class) => immediate pause all lifecycle sends until fixed.

### Support load
- Activation-related ticket volume: **> +20% vs trailing 2-week baseline** AND tagged to onboarding/activation => review within 24h.
- If tickets contain compliance concerns or repeated “stop emailing me” => immediate escalation.

### Console performance
- Dashboard/console p95 page load time: **no worse than +5%** vs control.
- Error rate for key onboarding routes: **no worse than +0.2pp absolute**.
- If regression persists > 2 hours after rollout => rollback flag.

## Reporting plan / deliverables
- Daily: lightweight snapshot in #growth + #product (Activation @24h, TTFS, guardrails)
- Twice weekly: deep-dive cut (new vs returning, SDK, region, model family)
- Final readout: sprint readout template + decision per lever (ship/iterate/rollback) + backlog

## Required dashboards / queries
- Experiment assignment table validation
- Activation funnel by cohort + arm
- TTFS distribution (median/p75) by arm
- D7/D14 retention by arm
- Guardrails panels (unsubscribe, tickets, console perf)

## Open questions
1) Confirm baseline activation rate (latest 4-week average) to finalize absolute pp thresholds.
2) Confirm eligibility rules for “activated already” returning users in console.
3) Confirm which events define “usage” for D7 (any request success vs any token usage).

## Acceptance criteria
- [ ] Primary/secondary metrics and windows documented and aligned with PM-412 definition
- [ ] Guardrail thresholds documented + owners + rollback triggers
- [ ] Sample size heuristics documented with clear caveats
- [ ] Decision rubric (ship/iterate/rollback) approved by Growth (Ben) + Product (Marissa) + Data (Mei/Sana)
- [ ] Link to final dashboards/query set included

comments: 2025-01-16 — Sana Farid: Drafted decision rubric + placeholder MDE targets. Waiting on Mei Lin to confirm current baseline activation @72h for self-serve signups (last 28d) so we can convert relative lifts into pp thresholds.

2025-01-17 — Ben Carter: +1 on ITT reads for email sequence. For email ship threshold, can we set +6% relative instead of +8%? Email changes are lower risk vs console changes; would rather keep them running if guardrails are clean.

2025-01-18 — Marissa Cole: For console performance guardrail, please call out which pages/routes are monitored (home dashboard, project setup, API keys). Also confirm rollback is feature-flag only; no code deploy required.

2025-01-19 — Sean Gallagher: Proposed SLO guardrails look reasonable. I’d prefer p95 rather than p99 for page load due to noise; add note that any error rate regression >0.2pp on onboarding routes triggers rollback within 2h.

2025-01-20 — Tyler Benson: Deliverability guardrails: unsubscribe threshold aligns w/ our prior sequences. Please add explicit: if we detect suppression failure (opt-out still receiving), we pause all sends immediately and notify Legal/Compliance channel.
2025-01-21 — Henry Cho: Marking as In Review. Once baseline is confirmed, lock final thresholds and paste into sprint tracker as the single source of truth for ship/iterate decisions.
